visualReview.notes: Inspected the perspective preview, four turns, and detailed renders of the granite wall and vaulted gate, the basilica flanked by the bell tower and minaret, the upper arcade, and the terraced ranges. The stepped granite walls, two distinct towers and broadly rising courtyard silhouette are recognizable in the final renders.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all nine shared viewing-date images. The imported granite, plaster, dressed stone, wood and roofing materials display with the expected bindings. The bounded dated geographic fixture loads and unloads successfully. The source terrain is assessed in the separate unmasked capture.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all twenty-five contexts and detail-level views. Every level retains the enclosure, its projections, the basilica, and separate towers. The street and closeup levels retain the real gate opening, paired belfry arches, minaret balcony, timber gallery bays and upper arcades.

geographicReview.notes: Fourteen native features set the monastery alignment, structure footprints and granite wall path. Inspected the original unmasked Sinai field and the foundations in the terrain-backed review. The walls are retained against the steep natural grade. Courtyard and visitor approach terraces are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The fortified Saint Catherine’s Monastery as seen in April 2011, including the granite curtain walls, entrance and buttresses, Transfiguration Basilica, bell tower, Fatimid mosque with minaret, Kléber Tower and the mapped ranges inside the enclosure.
fidelityReview.notes: The exact Qualla panorama establishes the warm battered granite, rounded gate-side tower, narrow gate, upper recessed arches, gray-green basilica roof, warm campanile and pale separate minaret. The UNESCO nomination gives the 2.25 m thickness and describes the narrow gate and vestibule. Local crown heights and interior terracing remain estimated.

imageryReview.notes: The 2011 Qualla panorama by Egghead06 is own work and was released under CC0. The exact Qualla file matches the native Commons hash and was inspected at its full resolution. The second local exterior candidate has conflicting capture dates and was excluded.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: April 2011 Saint Catherine’s Monastery at Mount Sinai, with its fortification, basilica, bell tower, Fatimid mosque and minaret, Kléber Tower and enclosed terraced ranges.

limitations: The natural field is retained as sampled. Its grid does not represent masonry courtyard terraces, survey elevations or the paths below the wall.

Native geometry controls the building footprints and most of the outer wall. Wall thickness follows the UNESCO nomination. Local crown profile, buttress projections, narrow entrance and lower retaining wall geometry are estimates matched to the panorama.

Basilica, cloister ranges, minaret and bell tower use estimated ridge heights and simplified openings. A courtyard gallery is reconstructed from the visible elevations and surrounding native boundaries.
The model represents the exterior in April 2011. Small inscriptions, interior chapels, the orchard, and later visitor paths are outside the modeled scope.
